Holkar @ Holkariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8
September, 2025

Author: Vivek Rusia
Bench: Vivek Rusia
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:25431
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Before

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'Ble
Shri Justice
Vivek Rusia

&
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Jai Kumar Pillai
 On The 8 th Of September, 2025
 Criminal Appeal No. 545 of 2017
 Holkar @ Holkariya
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Vivek Singh - Senior Advocate alongwith Shri Raj
 Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Surendra Kumar Gupta - Government Advocate for t
 respondent / State.
 Order
Per: Justice Vivek Rusia

Instead of hearing on the application for suspension of jail sentence (I.A.
No. 12314 of 2025), this criminal appeal is heard finally with the consent of both the parties.

02. The appellant has filed the present criminal appeal under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, against the judgement of conviction and sentence dated 15.02.2017 passed by the First Additional Sessions Judge, Alirajpur (M.P.) in Special Sessions Trial No. 04/2015, whereby he has been convicted for commission of offences punishable under Sections 363 & 366 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25431 2 CRA-545-2017 with a fine of Rs. 1,000/- and R.I. for 4 years with a fine of Rs. 1,000/-, respectively,
and Section 5/6 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences, 2012, and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life with a fine of Rs. 2,000/- with default stipulations.
03.

entities.text: Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, the appellant abducted the prosecutrix (PW/5) on 25.05.2015, and thereafter, she was returned back to home.

A missing person report was lodged by her father,
followed by an FIR No.160/2016 under Section 363 of IPC dated 19.10.2013.

According to the Holkar @ Holkariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41153685/
1 complaint, Chamariya's daughter went to the house of a relative on 25.05.2012 and did not return home till night, and he has an apprehension that she has eloped with local villager named Holkar i.e.
the appellant.

entities.text: Holkar @ Holkariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The prosecutrix was recovered on 01.01.2015, and the appellant was arrested on 02.01.2015.
Thereafter, the offences under Sections 366, 376, 506 of IPC and Section 3/5(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012, were also added in the FIR.
She was medically examined by a lady doctor, but no definite opinion about the commission of rape was given in the MLC.
Her date of birth was found to be 01.03.1996 as per entries in the school scholar register.
Undisputedly, she lived along with the appellant for 3 years and delivered a baby girl.
The FSL report has been found positive, which the appellant is not assailing in this appeal.

04. Shri Vivek Singh, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that as per the testimony of PW/1, she was a consenting party; the age has not been found proved by reliable documentary evidence like a birth certificate.

As per the x-ray report, she was found to be above 18 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25431 3 CRA-545-2017 years of age; thus, the appellant has wrongly been convicted under Section 376 of the IPC and Section 5/6 of the POSCO Act, 2012.
The appellant has undergone more than 10 years of a jail sentence.
As per the school record, her date of birth was 01.03.1996; therefore, at the time of missing on 25.05.2012, she was aged about 16 years, 1 month and 24 days.
She lived for 3 years with this appellant, and when she was examined on 02.01.2015, she was more than 18 years of age.
As per her court's statement, after living 3 years with the appellant, she delivered a child.
05. As per the doctor's opinion, the age of the child is 1 year, and she must have delivered the child at the age of 17 to 18 years.

Ramsingh, a teacher, brought the scholar register from the school,
according to which the prosecutrix was given admission on 09.07.2002 and studied till 01.07.2008.
In cross-examination he admitted that he has not brought any certificate on the basis of which the date of birth was recorded, and he is not the person who recorded the date of birth in the register.
Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove the date of birth 01.03.1996 from any authentic documents.
The doctor, Kailash Chandra Gupta, assessed the prosecution's age of more than 18 years on the basis of x-ray report.
Apart from that, Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, was amended by Act of 25 of 2019 w.e.f. 16.08.2019, whereby the minimum punishment of 20 years has been prescribed.
Before such an amendment, the minimum punishment was only 10 years, which may extend to imprisonment for life with a fine.

06. Shri Vivek Singh, learned senior counsel for the appellant, submits that the appellant is not assailing the convictions of the appellant on merit; he NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25431 4 CRA-545-2017 is assailing only the sentence of life which has wrongly been awarded to the appellant.

Therefore, it is prayed that the convictions under Sections 363 & 366 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 be maintained, but the said sentence should be reduced to 10 years, which was the minimum sentence at the time of commission of the crime.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the entire record.
07. Admittedly, in this case, the offence was committed prior to 16.08.2019; therefore, the minimum sentence which could have been awarded to the appellant was 10 years.

The learned trial Court has Holkar @ Holkariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41153685/
2 awarded the sentence of life on 15.02.2017 without assigning any reason; thus, when the exact age of the prosecutrix has not been found proved, coupled with the fact that there is not an exact date of commission of the sexual offence, then the imprisonment of a life sentence should not have been awarded to the appellant.

entities.text: Holkar @ Holkariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant belongs to the Bhil community in which marriage by way of Bhagora is very common and in practice.
At the time of the offence, the appellant was also aged about 23 years with no criminal record.
As per his defence and as per customs prevailing in the Bhil community, he ran away with the prosecutrix and lived as husband and wife.
08. In view of the above, the criminal appeal is partly allowed.
So far as the culpability of the appellant is concerned, the same is maintained, but the conviction is reduced from life imprisonment to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.

The rest of the sentence under Sections 363 &
366 of the IPC is maintained and has already been undergone.

Since the appellant has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25431 5 CRA-545-2017 already undergone 10 years of a jail sentence, therefore, he shall be released forthwith (if he is not required in any other case).
09.
Let the record of the trial Court be sent back along with the photocopy of this judgement.
Certified copy, as per rules.
